title: Activepieces vs Windmill: Pricing and Features (2026)
summary: Activepieces vs Windmill both automate workflows but target different team types and budgets. This comparison shows which platform matches your needs.
body_markdown:
## Who builds workflows in your team


Activepieces suits teams where operations and business staff build and maintain automations, with 746 integrations to build from. Windmill suits teams where engineers do, because the unit of work differs: a visual workflow with connectors in one, a script in the other.


### Activepieces: visual builder and integrations


In Activepieces, you build a flow on a canvas.


A trigger starts it, and each step after it is an integration, one of 746 and roughly 60% of them community-contributed: a packaged connector for an app or a built-in utility, with its actions exposed as forms to fill in, which means the connector you need probably already exists.


Nobody has to read an API reference to add a row to a spreadsheet.


In the screenshot's test flow, a Schedule trigger labelled "Every Hour" is selected, and an integration selector lists spreadsheet integrations (Google Sheets, Microsoft Excel 365, AITable, Retable) with actions such as Insert Row, Update Row and Find Rows.


The settings panel carries a "Run on weekends" toggle and a sample-data test that returned successfully. Take from it that scheduling, app choice and testing all happen in one screen, with no code written.


You don't hire for this, you describe it: type the process into the built-in chat and Activepieces builds and publishes the flow, the same artifact someone would have assembled on the canvas, with no engineer in the loop.


The published flow sits under the same RBAC and audit logs as every hand-built one, and each run leaves a trace that someone in finance or operations can read without any certification.


Describe a process that touches your connected apps and the result is a live flow in your account, with a run trace showing what happened. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


### Windmill: scripts, workflows and apps


Windmill starts from the script. You write a function in a supported language, and Windmill supplies the surrounding machinery: a generated input form, a schedule, a permissions model and a run history. Flows chain scripts together, and apps put a user interface over them.


Because every step is code, you can version, review and test it like any other. An engineer gets that rigour, and a non-engineer gets a wall.


### Verdict on who should build


**Choose by who will own the automation** after the first version ships. If operations or business staff own it, the visual builder keeps changes in their hands.


> An engineer gets that rigour, and a non-engineer gets a wall.


If engineers own it and want scripts reviewed like the rest of the codebase, Windmill matches how they already work.
